objectClass.notes: A portrait mobile-game environment reconstructed as a code-native procedural Three.js world around HabitGame's renderer-owned canonical 36-tile board. Visible source geometry is authoritative; hidden/rear forms remain labelled inference.

reasoning: The source combines a continuous floating cliff shell, dense central fortress, four landmark families, a volcanic horizon, liquid/effect layers, and a multi-stage mission hierarchy.
Fidelity depends on deep attachment ownership, visible route clearance, repeated masonry/iron/rune systems, independent PBR responses, and cross-view volume inferred from one source.
The approved 32-part Gauntlet inventory and mobile action-ready requirements place this at the ultra-complex tier.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Ultra-complex is required by the observed architectural density, 32 approved production entries, multiple motion/socket systems, seven material families, phone-scale fidelity requirement, and single-view occlusion risk.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: Rear citadel elevation and hidden arena interior are not visible; use secondary-inferred construction references and medium confidence.
The complete underside and rear lava-channel continuity are inferred from the visible front and lateral falls.
Bridge hinge, chain-drum, and counterweight geometry is mission-driven secondary inference, not source-visible fact.
The Pyre Sentinel guardian is absent from the source and remains locked until its own approved secondary-inferred identity packet.
The source's approximate route and baked Island 043 UI are excluded; canonical runtime Island 020 and the 36 renderer-owned tiles govern.

details.description: Branching recessed lava seams descend the tall far volcanic peak and split into smaller tributaries.
details.affects: far-horizon peak silhouette and emissive depth

details.description: Uneven horizontal and diagonal basalt terrace ridges step toward the glowing ravines.
details.affects: far terrain depth and grazing highlights

details.description: A pointed iron teardrop frame surrounds a real open flame aperture with a thick beveled collar.
Narrow vertical tower piers carry real chamfered edges that catch orange grazing light above deep recesses.
details.affects: central tower verticality and material separation

details.description: Cooled black crust forms irregular raised lips and downward teeth around hot molten overhangs.
The side brazier uses a low circular bowl ringed by short black iron spikes and a bright central flame.
Sparse embers vary in size and value across near, middle, and far smoke layers rather than forming a uniform field.
Front-left cliff columns break into nonuniform vertical facets with missing corners along the silhouette.
Heavy oval iron chain links hang vertically from the outer cliff with visible interlocking rotation and irregular soot.
A rare cool cyan circular beacon sits inside a brass-rimmed stone socket, balancing the dominant orange palette.
details.affects: cool accent hierarchy and side-platform identity

details.description: Connected low labyrinth walls have thick cap blocks with recessed joints, chipped corners, and orange cavity spill.
details.affects: citadel maze hierarchy and phone readability

details.description: Tall amber window slits are deep openings behind narrow iron/stone frames, not flat orange decals.
details.affects: tower depth and emissive scale hierarchy

details.description: Molten channels have narrow cooled crust borders that vary in width and expose brighter yellow cores at constrictions.
Front radial stairs use thick treads with chipped beveled noses, dark risers, and orange contact light.
Small aged-brass studs repeat along the route rim at regular spacing with brighter crowns and darker recesses.
details.affects: route material identity without replacing canonical tiles

details.description: A broad orange lavafall drops from a visible channel mouth down a deeply faceted lateral cliff and narrows between rock ribs.
The dark orange egg carries irregular bright molten cracks separated by raised cooled shell islands.
The major front lavafall uses a yellow-orange central hot core, darker red margins, and black cooled ledges interrupting the flow.
details.affects: front focal hierarchy and floating-island depth

details.description: Black soot and warm brown patina concentrate in masonry cavities, under iron collars, and around flame-adjacent recesses.
Aged orange-gold trim shows bright edge wear on raised rims and darker brown patina in recessed seams near braziers and banners.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At the matched portrait overview, the complete renderer-owned 36-tile route circles a deep floating basalt island whose tall central Crucible Citadel, connected labyrinth walls, lavafalls, volcanic horizon, and five stable landmark sockets reproduce the source's immediate silhouette and value hierarchy.

The central Citadel representative slice holds as true volume from source, left, right, rear, and top-clearance views before wider production; no camera-dependent facade, disconnected masonry, route collision, or flat underside is accepted.

Every landmark is a coherent additive L1-L3 family, every mission bridge accumulates from canonical committed state, every moving part has pivots/sockets/colliders, and reduced motion reaches the identical settled world state.
Obsidian, basalt, iron, aged brass, soot, and magma remain materially distinct under reference-matched and neutral/grazing light while emissive lava preserves black-stone form and phone readability.

featureGroups.name: Floating island silhouette, depth, and route clearance
qualityCriteria: The island reads as one deep supported volcanic mass with stepped terraces, jagged underside, broad front lavafall cuts, and asymmetric cliff breaks.
The full canonical route remains visible and quiet at 390x844 with no terrain, wall, bridge, or landmark intrusion.
failureModes: flat disc or disconnected rock pile replaces the deep source silhouette
route, landmark doors, or token path are obscured
lavafalls start or end in mid-air

featureGroups.name: Crucible Citadel tower, connected maze, gates, and arena identity
qualityCriteria: A tall narrow keep dominates connected stepped curtain walls and buttresses embedded in a radial arena foundation.
Every gate is a physical throughpass with plausible rear volume; the fortress is not a stack of disconnected boxes or a one-camera facade.
failureModes: tower loses dominance or reads as a generic castle
maze walls are loose cuboids without connected courts
rear/profile collapses or gates are painted recesses

featureGroups.name: Landmark foundations, lava channels, and Firebridge attachments
qualityCriteria: Every landmark foundation is buried into one owned terrace collar and remains within its footprint through L1-L3.
Each Firebridge connects paired landings through declared hinge and chain sockets; the complete swept envelope clears route, gates, cameras, and all L3 shells.
failureModes: bridge pivots from its center instead of its hinge
chain endpoints separate or machinery intersects
construction robots enter landmark or route collision volumes

featureGroups.name: Obsidian, basalt, iron, brass, soot, and magma response
qualityCriteria: Dark mineral, worked stone, black iron, aged brass, soot, cooled crust, and molten cores remain visually distinct through independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, AO, and emissive channels.
Macro strata, meso masonry/chipping, and micro pitting/edge wear survive neutral and grazing light; emissive spill never replaces material response.
failureModes: all dark surfaces read as uniform glossy plastic
magma becomes flat orange paint or blows out adjacent form
one texture is aliased across unrelated PBR channels

featureGroups.name: Action-ready build, mission, interaction, and reduced-motion hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Named roots, pivots, sockets, colliders, focus anchors, part-picking/explode metadata, LOD groups, and disposal hooks cover every approved production part.
Mission state commits through the canonical mutex-protected action before cinematic playback; four bridge stages are monotonic, replayable, interrupt-safe, and save-compatible.
Resting, working, commissioning, ambience, and reduced-motion modes converge on the same settled geometry without moving board, token, camera, funded meshes, or hit targets.
failureModes: UI or presentation layer owns gameplay progress
prior mission stages disappear or repeat after interruption
reduced motion reaches a different state
click/explode part definitions disagree or required parts are fused

visualDeltaChecks: floating-island silhouette, underside depth, and lavafall-mouth delta
citadel tower-to-route proportion and connected-maze negative-space delta
phone-readable repeated masonry, spikes, chains, braziers, windows, and rune distribution delta
canonical mission/build hierarchy, settled-state, and reduced-motion parity delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
